text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

SOYBEAN SALE - Exporters switched a sale of 108,000 tonnes of soybeans to Taiwan to U.S. origin, U.S. Agriculture Department said. The sale, for 1996-97 delivery, was originally reported as optional origin.

WHEAT SALES - South Korean feed milling companies bought 30,000 tonnes of Argentine feed wheat at $142.20 a tonne C and F, traders said. TradiGrain bought the grain through private negotiation last Thursday, with arrival by July 10 to the western port of Inchon.
WHEAT TENDERS - Iraq passed on offers to buy 50,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter wheat, European exporters said. The tender came under a U.N. oil-for-food deal.

- Sri Lanka's Co-operative Wholesale Establishment seeks 100,000 tonnes of hard wheat in 50,000-tonne lots, government officials said. Tenders close on May 16 with the first shipment for May 22-June 5 if from the U.S., Canada, Europe or Argentina, and June 10-19 from Australia or Saudi Arabia. The second shipment was for June 16-25 if from U.S., Canada, the Continent and Argentina, and June 30-July 9 from Australia and Saudi Arabia.

WHEAT TENDERS - South Korea's Cheiljedang Corp and Dongah Flour Mills Co Ltd jointly invited tenders to buy a total of 21,000 tonnes of U.S. No.1 wheat by 2:00 p.m. local time (0500 GMT) Wednesday, company officials said. Cheiljedang seeks 11,000 tonnes at basis prices over U.S. July futures. Dongah Flour seeks the balance at fixed prices. Shipment was for June 5-July 5 to the port of Inchon.
- Pakistan is likely to tender next week for 330,000 tonnes of soft white wheat for May-June delivery, a trade source in Islamabad said Friday.
WHEAT TENDERS - Jordan on May 1 will seek 120,000 tonnes of U.S. HRW and/or northern spring wheat for May/June.
CORN TENDER - The Commodity Credit Corp of the USDA said it would tender May 1 for up to 50,000 tonnes of U.S. corn for donation to North Korea. The corn is for May 10-30 shipment.
SOYBEAN TENDER - CCC was to tender April 30 for up to 10,000 tonnes of U.S. yellow soybeans for export to Ukraine, for May 10-June 5 shipment.
SOYMEAL TENDER - El Salvador is to tender April 28 for 8,000 to 10,000 tonnes of PL-480 soybean meal for May 7-22 shipment, the buyer's agent said.

COMMODITY TENDERS - South Korea's National Livestock Cooperatives Federation (NLCF) seeks to buy 50,000 tonnes of tapioca hard pellet at 11:00 a.m. local time (0200 GMT) Friday for June-September arrival, an NLCF official said. It also invites tenders to buy 30,000 tonnes of wheat bran pellet or rice bran pellet on the same day for July 10 and September 10 arrival. If NLCF passes in whole or part due to high prices, it will re-invite the tenders on May 6.

- The CCC said it will tender April 29 for pinto beans, sunflower oil, bulgur and wheat-soy blend for donation to Moldova. It seeks 255 tonnes of pinto beans, 605 tonnes of sunflower oil, 510 tonnes of bulgur (cracked wheat), and 255 tonnes of a wheat-soy blend. The beans, bulgur and wheat-soy blend were for June 6-20 shipment and the oil was for June 20-July 5.

MARKET TALK - USDA said Monday it released $205 million in PL-480 funds, including Food for Progress grants, to 21 countries for the third quarter of fiscal 1997. A planned commodity purchase being developed for the Philippines was changed from rice to soybean meal. The sale to the Philippines would involve about 15,100 tonnes of soybean meal worth $5 million. Food for Progress grants, which encourage free-market reforms, totaled $30 million, including to $15 million to Kyrgyzstan, $5 million to Mongolia and $10 million to Tajikistan, all for wheat flour. PL-480 funds for Title I for market development equal 479,600 tonnes of wheat, 46,600 tonnes of rice, 26,100 tonnes of vegetable oil, 129,900 tonnes of oilmeal and 2,400 tonnes of tallow...Hong Kong and China grains traders said they could not confirm U.S. soybean sales to China but added that while U.S. soybeans were more expensive than South American soybeans, a U.S. deal was not inconceivable... China expects to import about 1.0 million tonnes of rice this year, the People's Daily Overseas Edition said on Monday... China may export 3.0 million tonnes of 1996/97 maize and 1.5 million tonnes in 1997/98, while U.S. exports should rise to 50.8 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 45.7 million tonnes, Sparks Companies said Monday...The United States said Monday it would consider seriously any new U.N. food appeal for North Korea and urged other countries to contribute because the Stalinist state is facing a famine...USDA U.S. grain/soybean export inspections for week of April 24: soybeans 18.937 million bushels vs 8.904 million the previous week, wheat 9.871 million vs 16.350 million; corn 30.301 million vs 36.349 million, and sorghum 4.440 million vs 5.228 million.
